findings.details: TIFF and HEIC/HEIF use index zero without coalescing unrelated pages/images. The pinned HEIC reader exposes collection primary first. T030 stores an actual first-IFD RightTop orientation tag and asserts oriented dimensions plus asymmetric known pixels; T031 embeds an approved self-generated genuine two-top-level HEVC collection, independently reads both colors and tests both extensions through the actual decoder.

One stable snapshot supplies both full decoder-exposed ping count inspection and selected conversion. Nonzero native inspection, absent output, ambiguous row/count/dimension shape or mixed format fails the item before conversion. Relative-source log records count, selected one, omitted count, unit, policy and decoder. Full single-frame JPEG candidate decoding/final no-overwrite move remain required.

Exclusive attempt directory plus exact source-name CreateNew establishes file ownership only after reservation succeeds; FileShare.Read blocks cooperative writers while copying. Regular/reparse and expected source length/time checks precede and follow copy; copied length must match. Ownership is registered before copy errors so exact owned cleanup runs on failure. Reserved arrivals/unknown siblings survive, with nonrecursive directory removal failure surfaced. Conversion retries use separate last-candidate ownership and cannot delete/reuse the source snapshot.

Changes are exactly seven implementation paths. Existing CLI forms, callable boundary, BAT, verified dependency pins/bootstrap and Windows CI workflow are preserved. Ordinary JPEG/PNG/BMP and video conversion behavior/seams are unchanged. Naming/Preflight changes are narrow explicit controlled-codec inspection mocks, and actual HEVC coverage is mandatory in the separate Frames suite. Generator libraries/wheel are provenance only, absent runtime and CI dependency changes.

The default runner includes all twelve Frames cases alongside prior mandatory suites. Actual GIF/TIFF/WebP/HEVC integration cases assert source hashes/timestamps/attributes and exact output/file/scratch shape. Failure cases cover invalid inspection, real changed source length/time, controlled short-copy metadata, external snapshot arrival and unknown neighbor. Final targeted PS7/PS5.1 summaries were read as 12/12 zero skipped and match reviewed runtime/test hashes; full final desktop/CI gates are separate execution evidence owned by root.

Independent original RIFF parse found no VP8X or VP8L alpha, an opaque 16x12 first patch at 12,14 on 64x48 canvas and optional opaque-white ANIM background hint. Pinned native full read, define0/coalesce and independent Pillow12.3 already render RGB black padding before normalization. Initial white-alpha expectation was unsupported by the encoded fixture/installed decoder. This does not establish a normalizer first-frame/canvas-selection defect; black is not asserted as mandatory across every compliant viewer.

history_interpretation:
Four uncommitted targeted development runs are retained. The first PS7 run passed
6/12 and failed six assertions: an HEIF label expectation, two mock source-path
errors, recursive copied-metadata inspection, a cleanup warning expected as success,
and an unsupported white/transparent WebP expectation. Independent RIFF, pinned
decoder and Pillow inspection found the original WebP alpha-free; its optional
white animation-background hint did not establish white rendered padding. The
second PS7 run passed 11/12 and failed an alpha expression applied to an RGB-only
second frame. Corrected fixture/mock/oracle checks passed 12/12 in PS7-3 and PS5.1-1;
no runtime fix was required for those test-development failures. Raw summaries,
XML, consoles and saved source snapshots stay ignored with hashes; their end-of-run
source hashes do not establish an immutable clean execution revision. Separately,
the native HEIC encode probe and first unpacked generator DLL import failed during
fixture tooling development; verified once-only generation and independent actual
two-image decoding then succeeded. These tooling events are distinct from runtime
assertion results and from the subsequent clean committed full acceptance runs.

independent_webp_diagnosis.classification: The encoded first fragment contains no alpha; the installed decoder already exposes a full RGB canvas with black padding before normalizer operations. The initial white/transparent expectation was unsupported by this actual encoded fixture. It does not establish a normalizer first-frame or canvas-selection defect.
independent_webp_diagnosis.qualification: ANIM background is an optional viewer hint, so opaque black padding is an observation of the pinned decoder/Pillow path, not an assertion that every compliant viewer must show black. The final regression requires real decoded alpha before expecting white flattening.

sources.finding: VP8X alpha indicates frame transparency; ANMF no-alpha content is opaque within its rectangle; ANIM background may fill canvas but viewers are not required to use its hint.
ReadSingleWEBPImage obtains alpha_trait from encoded fragment; the first animation image is expanded to canvas and pixels outside fragment are zeroed. An alpha-free fragment leaves an RGB canvas.
Reference animation decoder clears key-frame canvas to transparent zeros and decodes at the frame offset; background is exposed in info without mandatory fill in this decoder.

details: The HEIF alias fixture expected HEIC metadata, while the actual pinned decoder reported HEIF for the .heif path; the test now asserts that actual alias.
Length and timestamp mutation mocks used a dynamically shadowed source path and acted on the report directory; the test retains an immutable trace.SourcePath.
The short-copy Get-Item mock recursed into itself and reached call-depth overflow; the fixture now uses IO.FileInfo for the narrowly controlled observation.

The unknown-neighbor cleanup case expected exit 0 although the completed output correctly retained an unknown neighboring file and reported partial cleanup with exit 2; the assertion now expects that warning.

The initial WebP first-pixel oracle expected a white alpha canvas although the encoded first fragment was opaque: VP8X flags 2, VP8L alpha_used false, and an opaque 16x12 fragment at offset 12,14. Independent raw/coalesced decoding had RGB black padding; the white ANIM background hint did not establish the intended transparent first frame. The fixture was revised to retain actual first-frame alpha and require decoded sRGBA channels plus a transparent corner before judging white JPEG output.

The revised WebP fixture had a transparent sRGBA first frame, but the test queried fx alpha on the RGB-only second frame and assumed 1; the observed expression was 0.12549. The corrected oracle inspects actual first-frame channels and its transparent pixel without making an unsupported RGB-only alpha assumption.
Both targeted editions passed after fixture/mock/oracle corrections; no runtime change was required to address these test-development failures.

limitations: Tooling-development native HEIC encode and unpacked generator DLL-resolution failures are recorded separately in the fixture provenance manifest.
Full raw failure messages contain local paths and remain in ignored console/XML artifacts; only qualified diagnoses are exported.

Actual T031 HEIC/HEIF evidence is a genuine two-image top-level still collection through two aliases. Timed HEIC animation, thumbnails, auxiliary images and arbitrary codec builds remain unverified; container counts describe only images exposed by the pinned decoder. The pinned native build reads HEIC/HEIF but cannot generate the fixture; one verified official development wheel produced the synthetic bytes in ignored scratch, with no installation, runtime/CI generator dependency or distributed generator binary.

Snapshot length/modification-time checks and duplicate keys are stability heuristics, not proof of content identity. General native argument/input-grammar safety and source changes retaining identical metadata remain outside this narrow neutral-snapshot policy. Owned cleanup deliberately preserves unknown entries and may return partial exit 2 after a valid JPEG has finalized.

Tagged colour/profile conversion before metadata removal is next M2-T02. Broader alpha/colour/reference fidelity, size-search quality, process timeout/resource budgets, cancellation, reporting and publication remain later tasks. Automated internal peer review does not grant owner aesthetic acceptance or authorize merge, release, deployment, tags or default-branch changes.
